It offers a free public tour and a free architecture tour

name: Carlton Gardens

facts.claim: 26-hectare Victorian-era gardens around the Royal Exhibition Building and Melbourne Museum
Part of the UNESCO-listed Royal Exhibition Building and Carlton Gardens World Heritage site

name: Melbourne Park

facts.claim: Home of the Australian Open tennis since 1988, beside Jolimont Yard
Rod Laver Arena seats about 15,000 and hosts concerts as well as tennis

name: Albert Park and Lake

facts.claim: 225-hectare urban park around an artificial lake, 3 km south of the CBD
A 4.7 km walking track circles the lake, with views back to the city skyline
Hosts the Albert Park Circuit of the Australian Grand Prix since 1996

name: Block Arcade

facts.claim: Built 1891-93 to designs by Twentyman & Askew, listed on the Victorian Heritage Register
Mosaic tiled floors, glass canopy and an octagonal rotunda link Collins and Elizabeth Streets
Home to The Tea Rooms 1892, the original Hopetoun Tea Rooms

name: Royal Arcade

facts.claim: Opened in 1870, the oldest surviving arcade in Australia, designed by Charles Webb
Gog and Magog figures strike the bells of Gaunt's clock each hour
Links Bourke Street Mall, Little Collins Street and Elizabeth Street
